主要内容: Murray Energy, a major U.S. coal mining company, has emerged from federal bankruptcy protection under a new name and ownership group. The company's Chapter 11 bankruptcy plan was approved in U.S. bankruptcy court in Ohio and became effective on September 16, 2020. Murray Energy Holdings completed the sale of its assets to an entity formed by former creditors, and the new company, American Consolidated Natural Resources Inc. (ACNR), is now the largest privately owned U.S. coal operator. ACNR operates active mines in Alabama, Kentucky, Ohio, West Virginia, and Utah, and has management services agreements to operate Foresight Energy mines in Illinois and Murray Energy subsidiary Murray Metallurgical mines. The restructuring eliminated over $8 billion in debt and legacy liabilities, providing ACNR with enhanced financial flexibility. Robert Moore, who replaced Robert Murray as CEO in 2019, now leads the new company, which has over 4,000 employees. The bankruptcy filing marked a significant political failure for President Donald Trump, who had sought to end what he called a 'war on coal' by Democrats. ACNR has also hired members of the United Mine Workers union, who formerly worked at Murray Energy.
